Executive Summary
Nutrien
Leal Terminal

Background

Nutrien Leal Terminal receives anhydrous ammonia from rail tankcars and/or tank trucks and dispenses anhydrous ammonia to tank trucks, truck dock loading arm consist of excess flow valves, for fertilizer application.  Both of the transfer processes are accomplished with ammonia transfer pump(s) and/or ammonia compressor(s).  The Leal Terminal also stores liquid anhydrous ammonia in an above ground storage tank (AST) within its facility.  The AST is surrounded by a containment dike, which is approximately 9 feet in height and has an interior area of 207,025 square feet.  The containment dike is visually inspected monthly and an professional certified survey is completed annually.   

The liquid anhydrous ammonia is stored in AST by refrigeration and in the ammonia bullet and railcars under pressure.  The AST has a capacity of 40,000 tons and 14 railcars containing 80 tons each can be stored on the rail spur.  As the results, the maximum amount of anhydrous ammonia that could be stored in the Leal Terminal is 41,500 tons.  Propane is stored in a AST with a capacity of 76,000 pounds.  The propane is used for heating product for loading, flare operation, and building heating. 

Rationale for Risk Management Program Development, Implementation, and Update

The 1990 Amendments to the Clean Air Act (CAA) require Environmental protection Agency EPA) to issue a rule specifying the type of actions to be taken by facilities to prevent accidental releases of substances into the atmosphere and reduce their potential impact on the public and the environment.  As the results of the 1990 Amendments, EPA issued the "Chemical Accident Prevention Provisions" (part 68 of Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR)) that requires affected facilities to develop and implement a risk management program.  The affected facilities include any facilities that handle, manufacture, store, or use above the specified threshold quantities o

f toxic substances in a process, including ammonia.  The threshold quantities for ammonia to trigger the development and implementation of a risk management program are 10,000 pounds.

The risk management program is designed to prevent accidental releases of substances that can cause serious harm to the public and the environment from short-term exposures and to mitigate the severity of releases that does occur. Since Nutrien is handling more than 10,000 pounds of ammonia, it is required to develop and implement a risk management program.  To comply with the RMP rules, Nutrien implemented an RMP program at the Leal Terminal and submitted an RMP to EPA in 1999.  The Nutrien's risk management program includes an offsite consequence analysis of a potential accidental release, a five-year accident history, a release prevention program, and an emergency response program.

The RMP rules required that the RMP be updated at least every five years.  Nutrien is updating the RMP for the Leal Terminal to comply with the rules.  

Five Year Accident History

The five-year accident history involves an examination of the effects of any accidental releases of anhydrous ammonia in the five years prior to the RMP update.  The five-year accident history covers:

	- the release of ammonia from Natalie's facility.
	- the release that caused at least one of the following:
		- On site deaths, injuries, or significant property damage (40 CFR
		  part 68.42(a)); or
		- known offsite deaths, injuries, property damage, environmental 
		  damage, evacuations, or sheltering in place (40 CFR Part 68.42
		  (a)).

During the last five years, the Leal Terminal has had no releases that caused death, injuries, property damage, or environmental damage either on or off site.

Release Prevention Program

Nutrien has a Release Prevention Program (RPP) in placed to prevent accidental releases of hazardous materials at this facility.  The RPP include:

	Process Safety Information (PSI)
	Nutrien has develo

ped and will keep current working copies of the PSI including information pertaining to the hazards of the process, the technology of the process, and equipment of the process.  All employees are trained in the operation of the entire terminal and all contractors are given training before performing work in the terminal.  The PSI will enable the employees and contractors of Nutrien to identify and understand the hazards posed by the process involving anhydrous ammonia.
	
 	Process Hazard Analysis (PHA)
	Nutrien is committed to performing PHA to identify, evaluate, and control hazard associated with the Nutrien's operations.  The PHA is to analyze the potential mishaps, identify the mishaps that could occur, analyze the likelihood that mishaps will occur, evaluate the consequence of these mishaps, and analyzed the likelihood that safety systems, mitigation systems, and emergency systems will function properly to eliminate or reduce the consequences of a mishap.
	
	The PHA will be updated at least every five (5) years to assure that the PHA is consistent with the current process.  The PHA was last updated in September 2021.  
	
	Operating Procedures (OPs)
	Nutrien is committed to the development of OPs to assure safe work practices are maintained.  The OPs are reviewed after unsafe work practice occurs.  The unsafe work practice is investigated and the OPs will be revised to reflect the unsafe practices.  The OPs was last updated January, 2022.
	
	Training
	Nutrien is committed to provide its employee's comprehensive training to assure that the work force can perform their duties safely, efficiently, and effectively.  Each employee has a training file that keeps track of his training requirement.  All of the employees at the Leal Terminal was last trained in February 2022.
	
	Mechanical Integrity (MI)
	Nutrien has developed a written program of maintaining of the MI of process equipment at the Leal Terminal.  The MI program includes pressure vessels and storage tanks,

piping systems and ancillary equipment, relief and vent systems and devices, emergency shutdown systems, controls, and pumps.  All equipment are inspected/tested at a frequency recommended by the manufacturer.  The equipment tested most recently is the Ammonia Cold Pumps February 2022. 
	
	Incident Investigation
	Nutrien has communicated to all of its employees that it is every employee's responsibility to report incidents and near misses to their immediate supervisor.  After an incident is reported, an incident investigation team which includes the employees involved in the incident will initiate an incident investigation.  The incident will also be input into a computer program celled 
ETQ that ties to the Nutrien corporate office.  The leader of the incident investigation team is knowledgeable of the plant and have received formal training in incident investigation.
	
	Compliance Audit
	A compliance audit of the Nutrien facility will be conducted at least every three (3) years to evaluate compliance of Nutrien's process with the release prevention program (RPP).  The audit team will include one person knowledgeable in audit skills and techniques and team members with appropriate technical expertise.  A compliance audit of the Leal Terminal was completed on September 2021.
	
	Management of Change (MOC)
	Nutrien's MOC system was developed to ensure that changes at Nutrien will not result in undetected unsafe situations and employees will be aware of all changes and their implications.  The Nutrien's MOC system includes the following considerations before any changes take place:
	
	- the authorization requirements for the change.
	- the technical basis for the proposed change
	- the impact of the change on health and safety.
	- the necessary time for the change.
	- required modification to Operating Procedures.
	
	After changes are made, all employees will be informed about the change and training will be provided to the employees prior to startup of the modified p

rocess.  In addition, the PSI and OP will be updated to reflect the changes made.  
	
	Pre-Startup Review (PSR)
	When change to the process is significant enough to require a change in safety information under the MOC, Nutrien will conduct a PSR.  The PSR Team Leader will develop a checklist and assemble team of key personnel to go over every element on the checklist during the PSR.  All PSR team members will be knowledgeable about the process and trained in the area of change.  
	
	Contractors
	Nutrien has developed and implemented safe work practices to control the entrance, presence and exit of contract employees in the terminal.  It is Nutrien's policy to select safe contractors, provide appropriate safety related information to contractors, develop safe work practices related to contractors and periodically evaluate contractors.  
	
	Employee Participation
	Nutrien is committed to involving employees and their representatives on the conduct and development of PHA and on the development of the other elements of plant safety, process safety management, and risk management planning.  Nutrien encourages employees to read, review and provide comments on all PSM/RMP documents.  The PSM/RMP documents was last reviewed by an Nutrien Leal Terminal's employee on January 2022.
	
	Hot Work Permits
	Hot work is defined as work that could generate a flame, intense heat, or sparks as a result of electric or gas welding, cutting, blazing, abrasions or similar operations.  Permitting is completed for all required work on terminal grounds.

Nutrien is committed to the implementation of the RMP to ensure safe operations of its plant and to prevent accident. 

Emergency Response Program

Nutrien has an Emergency Action Program (EAP) in place to respond to releases of hazardous material at this facility.  All Nutrien employees work in conjunction with the local fire department and LEPC agencies.  All Nutrien employees are trained in first aid, CPR, and the use of AEDs.  

Nutrien w

orks closely with the local fire department and LEPC agencies in responding to site emergencies.  Nutrien continues to keep the fire department informed of any new hazardous materials that are introduced into the workplace.  The other outside agencies that will be involved in responding to emergencies at Nutrien include the County Sheriff, Highway Patrol, local hospital, and outside contractors that are needed for such operations as containment, cleanup, material handling, etc.

All reportable releases of hazardous material will be reported immediately to the National Response Center, State Emergency response Commission, and the Local Emergency Planning Committee.

Planned Changes to Improve Safety 

Process hazard analysis (PHAs), incident investigations, Management of Change, and compliance audits are conducted regularly at the Leal Terminal to identify potential hazards, learn from mistakes, verify design and maintain compliance. Equipment inspections, safety meetings, review of industry experiences, technology improvements, and employee suggestions also provide continuous improvement opportunities. As a result of these improvement opportunities recommendations are reviewed, corrective actions are developed and tracked to completion.  Affected personnel are informed of projects and corrective actions being incorporated at the Leal Terminal.     
The Leal Terminal has a 5-Year Capital Plan includes an electrical system and instrumentation/controls project improve safety. The site has a plan to upgrade site switchgear and replace older MCCs.  The 5-Year Plan also includes projects to replace the NH3 Heater and replace the Propane Vaporizer.  This will also include piping upgrades at the rail unloading areas.
The terminal has also implemented a Potential Serious Injury and Fatality (PSIF) program.  This program focuses on routine tasks and hazards that have the potential to cause a life altering injury.  The site routinely conducts PSIF Audits across the facility, i
tems that are identified have corrective actions assigned and tracked to completion within our EtQ database.
